description: Add Goldsky GraphQL client for querying OrderFilledEvent data from the Polymarket orderbook subgraph
steps: Create src/prediction_data/bronze/polymarket/goldsky.py with GoldskyClient class
Implement GraphQL POST requests to https://api.goldsky.com/api/public/project_cl6mb8i9h0003e201j6li0diw/subgraphs/orderbook-subgraph/prod/gn
Implement id_gt cursor-based pagination for orderFilledEvents query (standard subgraph pattern: query first:1000, orderBy:id, where:{id_gt:$cursor})
Add timestamp filtering (timestamp_gte, timestamp_lte) to scope queries by day boundaries
Use existing httpx-based HTTP client (core/http.py) for retries and backoff
Add rate limiting between pages to respect Goldsky API limits
Add unit tests for GraphQL query construction, pagination, and response parsing

description: Add order_filled ingestion function that fetches OrderFilledEvents from Goldsky and writes to bronze S3
steps: Add ingest_order_filled() async function to polymarket/ingest.py
Compute day boundaries (start-of-day, end-of-day UTC) from --dt param as Unix timestamps
Use GoldskyClient to fetch all OrderFilledEvents for the day
Store raw subgraph response fields in camelCase (transactionHash, orderHash, timestamp, maker, taker, makerAssetId, takerAssetId, makerAmountFilled, takerAmountFilled, fee) as JSONL.gz
Upload to S3: bronze/polymarket/order_filled/dt={date}/run_id={uuid}/part-NNN.jsonl.gz
Generate manifest with api_base_url pointing to Goldsky endpoint, pagination='cursor'
Add run_ingest_order_filled() synchronous wrapper for CLI usage

description: Wire order_filled entity into CLI ingestion and backfill commands
steps: Add 'prediction-data ingest polymarket-order-filled --dt YYYY-MM-DD' command to cli/main.py
Register order_filled as a valid Polymarket entity in backfill CLI (--entity order_filled)
Route polymarket/order_filled in backfill _ingest_one() to ingest_order_filled()
Verify dry-run output includes order_filled when --entity all or --entity order_filled

description: Build script to convert existing S3 parquet data into bronze JSONL.gz format for historical backfill
steps: Create scripts/backfill_order_filled_from_parquet.py
Read parquet files from s3://polymarket-bcp892/raw/polymarket/order_filled/ using pyarrow
Convert fields: rename snake_case to camelCase (transaction_hash -> transactionHash, maker_asset_id -> makerAssetId, etc.)
Convert amounts: multiply float values by 1e6 and cast to int (e.g. 4.45 -> 4450000) to match subgraph base units
Convert timestamp: datetime -> Unix epoch integer (seconds)
Set missing fields to null: orderHash, fee, id
Write output as JSONL.gz to bronze bucket: bronze/polymarket/order_filled/dt={date}/run_id={uuid}/part-NNN.jsonl.gz
Generate manifest per day with source metadata indicating parquet backfill origin
Add --dry-run flag to preview conversion without writing to S3
Add --start-date / --end-date filtering to scope which days to convert

description: Test order_filled ingestion and parquet conversion end-to-end
steps: Add unit tests for GoldskyClient (query construction, pagination, timestamp filtering)
Add unit tests for order_filled ingestion (S3 key structure, manifest correctness)
Add unit tests for parquet-to-bronze field conversion (camelCase rename, amount scaling, timestamp conversion, null fields)
Add integration test for single-day Goldsky order_filled ingestion
Validate a Goldsky-ingested record vs a parquet-backfilled record to confirm schema alignment
Run full test suite: pytest -m 'not integration', mypy src/, ruff check src/ tests/

description: Document Goldsky subgraph integration, order_filled schema, and backfill procedures
steps: Update CLAUDE.md with Goldsky subgraph endpoint, OrderFilledEvent schema, and rate limits
Document order_filled CLI usage examples (ingest and backfill)
Document parquet backfill script usage with examples
Note schema differences between Goldsky-sourced and parquet-backfilled records (missing orderHash, fee, id)
